intended_object: The natural inclusion homomorphism 𝒪_K^× → K^{𝔪}, where K^{𝔪} is the subgroup of K^× of elements that are units (valuation 1) at every prime dividing the finite part of the modulus 𝔪. It is the map used in the ray class group exact sequence. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The definition takes the map (𝒪_K)ˣ → Kˣ induced by algebraMap and restricts its codomain to `primeToSubgroup 𝔪`. That subgroup is the S-unit subgroup for the complement of the support of 𝔪, i.e. the elements of valuation 1 at every prime dividing the finite part. The lemma `unitsMap_mem_primeToSubgroup` shows that a global unit has valuation 1 at every finite prime, which justifies the restriction. So the result is exactly the inclusion of 𝒪_K^× into K^{𝔪}. The number-field setting is the one in which the library defines `Modulus` (a finite part plus a set of real places), so the definition is not too narrow. Mathlib has no ray-class modulus or `primeToSubgroup` map of this kind.
